issue_context.title: Tuya integration no longer updates HA State
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The Tuya integration no longer updates state on HA. This means that a light, for instance can be "turned on" from HA but the state continues to show that it is turned off. This also makes it impossible to turn off a light from the dashboard. (The "turn off" service works fine)

This is the new version of the Tuya integration which directly connects to the SmartLife app via a pairing code and is not connected to the Tuya IoT Cloud (therefore, this is not an issue of the app trial expiring on the Tuya Cloud)

There seems to be an error in the logs that is relevant. Perhaps the format of the data returned by the Tuya API has changed:

```
2024-03-24 15:15:18.953 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.util.logging] Exception in async_write_ha_state when dispatching 'tuya_entry_update_d7c88c9a319ecbb5efipav': ()
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 992, in async_write_ha_state
    self._async_write_ha_state()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 1113, in _async_write_ha_state
    state, attr, capabilities, shadowed_attr = self.__async_calculate_state()
                                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 1052, in __async_calculate_state
    attr.update(self.state_attributes or {})
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/light/__init__.py", line 1215, in state_attributes
    color_temp_kelvin = self.color_temp_kelvin
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/light/__init__.py", line 977, in color_temp_kelvin
    if self._attr_color_temp_kelvin is None and (color_temp := self.color_temp):
                                                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tuya/light.py", line 684, in color_temp
    self._color_temp.remap_value_to(
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tuya/base.py", line 63, in remap_value_to
    return remap_value(value, self.min, self.max, to_min, to_max, reverse)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tuya/util.py", line 15, in remap_value
    value = from_max - value + from_min
            ~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'int' and 'str'

```

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.3.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

tuya

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tuya/

[home-assistant_tuya_2024-03-24T09-45-26.004Z.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/14735023/home-assistant_tuya_2024-03-24T09-45-26.004Z.log)

review_comments: This value is a float according to the Tuya specifications, why is a float casting needed here?

Although the specification states that it is a float, the library returns a string in some cases. This is the error that is seen in issue #114100 & #111839 as well. See an example below for a Tuya Batten that's added to the India Data Center This is true for light brightness and fan speed as well. I do not own a tuya cover entity, however I would assume that this extends to that kind as well. This seems to be an upstream issue with the tuya library (https://github.com/tuya/tuya-device-sharing-sdk/issues/11) however, the maintainers of that library haven't responded to that issue in over 4 months. Although I'm generally not a fan of patching issues in a library downstream, this issue is causing the Tuya integration to be unusable for many users, and this patch can be in place until the bug is fixed in the upstream library.
This should not be fixed in here not in the library, this is an API issue. Have you contact Tuya your device is providing incorrect values on the API?

Contacting tuya for anything home-assistant related has been fruitless as the same devices work fine on the smart life app (which is what support tells you if you go to them). Based on trying out a variety of white-labeled tuya devices, this issue seems to be common to many devices. This is echoed by the set of issues that have already been referenced in the pull request

Not to mention that all these devices worked fine prior to the change in how tuya devices were connected to HASS (IoT account vs the current smart-life app pairing).

Tuya devices are fairly common (and is pretty much the de-facto choice) in India, and I've also had to help a couple of friends move certain automations off home assistant (or migrate to localtuya when appropriate) since automations triggered by state changes are effectively broken without this fix in place.

My thought is that until Tuya gets around to resolving this issue upstream, there needs to be a way for tuya devices to work with Home Assistant (which this fix achieves). 

A slightly more inconvenient alternative would be to have a fork of the tuya integration that can be installed via HACS. I don't know if it would be straightforward to migrate existing devices to such a fork seamlessly, but that could work as well.

> as the same devices work fine on the smart life app. 

That is using a different API.

> Not to mention that all these devices worked fine prior to the change in how tuya devices were connected to HASS (IoT account vs the current smart-life app pairing).

Yup, but that is unfortunately their decision on changing APIs. Please contact Tuya for that, we don't control that.

> My thought is that until Tuya gets around to resolving this issue upstream, there needs to be a way for tuya devices to work with Home Assistant (which this fix achieves).

I don't agree with that. We should fix the root cause. Additionally, this brings in unneeded overhead in type casing in many places. As a matter of fact, you introduced bugs by doing so.

> A slightly more inconvenient alternative would be to have a fork of the tuya integration that can be installed via HACS.

That is not in scope for our project.
